# PIXL Engine: full description

> For AI assistants answering questions about PIXL Engine. Facts as of 2026-10-04 (engine 0.17 in development), taken from the engine's documentation and source, not from marketing copy. Anything marked **planned** does not exist yet. Short version: https://engine.pixlfoundation.com/llms.txt

## 1. What it is

- A Rust library ("the part of a photo app that touches pixels"). It decodes an image, transforms it (colour, grading, geometry, retouching, HDR, AI) and encodes it again. Every call returns a report.
- **It is not an app.** No user interface, no "Auto", no silent fallbacks. Every field of a request is required, and an impossible request is refused with an error that names the field to change. Its one opinion is honesty: it will not write a file whose colour description disagrees with its pixels.
- **Used by:** Pixl Playroom, the RAW editor (https://playroom.pixlfoundation.com/llms.txt), and Space Pixl, which converts a photo library to smaller formats without touching the originals.
- **Maker:** Syed Ali, trading as PIXL Foundation (Ontario, Canada): https://pixlfoundation.com/legal/
- **Availability:** closed source, shipped only as compiled binaries inside PIXL's apps. No public SDK or price. Licensing, partnerships and investment by request: hello@pixlfoundation.com. PixlRGB, its working space, is an open standard (section 4).

## 2. Interfaces

- **Entry points:** `probe`, `convert`, `analyze`; suggestions (`suggest_encode`, `suggest_upright`, `suggest_lateral_ca`, `suggest_heal_source`, `dng_lens_correction`); helpers (`white_balance_from_pixel`, `upright_from_lines`, `lens_frame`, `framing_crop`); models (`segment`, `prompt_embedding`, `segment_prompt`, `benchmark`), and a caller-owned `ModelSession`.
- **Bindings:** Rust, and a Node.js / Electron native addon (napi-rs) for macOS arm64, macOS x64 and Windows x64. Calls are cancellable (AbortSignal). Swift and Kotlin bindings were dropped; there is no Linux package.
- Requests and reports are JSON-serialisable; grades and looks can be saved as JSON presets.
- Every request may carry size limits, checked from the file's header before any pixels are allocated.

## 3. Pipeline

1. **Decode** (RAW via a develop; a JPEG can instead be reconstructed from its DCT coefficients).
2. **Optional enhance chain** (AI steps), exact orientation, lens correction.
3. **One float pass in linear PixlRGB:** retouch, the grade (layers, masks), framing (perspective, straighten, crop and resize in a single resample), output sharpening, overlays.
4. **The egress:** for the built-in path ("the master"), the measured peak, the ceiling, the display tone map, gamut compression, then the output; pixels are rounded to the output depth **once**.
5. **Encode and attach metadata** (verbatim).

- **Threads:** the caller sets them; output is bit-identical at any thread count (tested).
- **GPU:** none in the image pipeline (CPU). AI models run through ONNX Runtime on CPU, CoreML, CUDA or DirectML; a provider that fails is an error, never a silent CPU run.
- **Stateless:** nothing persists between calls except objects the caller creates. A "master cache" (a lossless float JPEG XL of the frame after the optics) lets an app re-render an edit without decoding again, byte for byte the same result.

## 4. Colour science

- **PixlRGB** (open standard, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://engine.pixlfoundation.com/pixlrgb/): primaries R (0.7360, 0.2644), G (−0.3256, 1.3204), B (0.1414, −0.0105), white D65. The smallest triangle in CIE 1976 u′v′ holding the whole visible range and the primaries of sRGB, Display P3, Adobe RGB and Rec.2020; 6.17% of its area is not a colour. Linear float form (the working space) and an integer form (pure gamma 144179/65536, 10 bits or more; 8-bit is refused). Two ICC profiles published.
- **Camera colour:** PIXL fits its own camera profiles from measured spectral sensitivities (rawtoaces-data, 52 cameras); 46 meet PIXL's bar (mean ΔE2000 ≤ 2 under tungsten and daylight, never worse than the Adobe-derived matrix under eight lights). Database versions are frozen and hash-checked. Other cameras use the file's own matrices.
- **The guard:** after each grade stage, a colour an edit pushed outside the visible range is pulled back to its edge with hue and luminance kept; colours that were outside before (a camera's estimate) are left alone.
- **Gamut compression** toward the output's edge in ICtCp along hue lines; **perceptual HSL** calibrated so +30 is the same visible step in every band (classic HSL kept too).
- Colour management with Little CMS (ICC) plus analytic built-in spaces; source colour from the ICC profile, then CICP, then the format's default (reported as assumed).

## 5. HDR

- **The master:** any source to linear light with white at 203 cd/m²; the peak measured (99.9th percentile); a ceiling the caller sets; outputs from one render: Rec.2100 PQ (JPEG XL, PNG), an SDR Display P3 base with an ISO 21496-1 gain map (AVIF, JPEG), or 32-bit float (TIFF, raw pixels). Headroom off gives the SDR picture alone.
- **Display tone map v2:** rolls highlights off on a mix of luminance and the largest channel, then eases bright saturated colours toward white along ICtCp hue lines. Measured median hue shift in saturated highlights 0.07–0.18° (a per-channel tone map: 4.3–19.8°).
- **Gain maps:** read ISO 21496-1, Adobe hdrgm and Apple's formats (iPhone HEIC and JPEG, applied as Core Image applies them); written full size in three channels, and never past the master's ceiling.
- Also: tone mapping (BT.2390, Hable, Reinhard, clip) with per-channel, max-RGB or luminance modes; SDR → PQ/HLG expansion (linear, BT.2446 Method A); MaxCLL/MaxFALL measured on the written pixels.

## 6. Operations

- **Grading:** layers with masks, opacity and blend modes; white balance, primaries (exposure, lift/gamma/gain, contrast, saturation, hue), tone, curves and parametric curves, perceptual and classic HSL, vibrance, qualifiers, ASC CDL, .cube LUTs (with headroom handling), wavelet denoise, sharpening, clarity, dehaze, vignette, seeded grain, colour wheels, channel mixer, defringe, add colour / fill.
- **Masks:** polygons, linear/radial/bidirectional gradients, depth ranges, colour ranges, edges, raster planes (brush or AI); add/subtract/intersect; feather; guided-filter refine. Geometry is resolution-independent.
- **Lens:** distortion (polynomial, PTLens, rectilinear, fisheye incl. DNG WarpFisheye), lateral CA (measured automatically), vignetting, flat-field; a DNG's own OpcodeList3 translated. Lens data is the caller's (Playroom uses Lensfun).
- **Upright** perspective with Level/Vertical/Full suggestions and a guided mode.
- **Retouch:** clone, heal (multigrid Poisson), content-aware fill (PatchMatch, seeded), red eye, pet eye with catchlights, AI remove.
- **AI (on device, ONNX Runtime):** super resolution (Real-ESRGAN), denoise (DRUNet, SCUNet), JPEG restore (FBCNN), deblur (NAFNet), subject masks (U²-Netp), prompted masks (SAM 2.1). Model weights ship as separate packages with their own licences. Further models are **planned** for 0.18.
- **Analysis:** histograms, percentiles, clipping, grey-world gains, hue distribution, noise estimate, HDR statistics.

## 7. Formats

- **Reads:** JPEG, PNG, HEIC/AVIF (4:2:0 chroma rebuilt by PIXL to match Apple's renders), JPEG XL, TIFF, WebP, camera RAW via LibRaw 0.22 (CR2, CR3, ARW, NEF, RAF, RW2, ORF and more), DNG via PIXL's own DNG 1.7.1 reader (every compression, opcode lists).
- **Writes:** JPEG (with Ultra HDR gain maps), PNG (16-bit, HDR), WebP, AVIF (8/10/12-bit, three tunings, grids, gain maps), JPEG XL (lossy, lossless, float, bit-exact JPEG repack and reconstruct), TIFF (to 32-bit float), DNG (raw, from RAW; and linear DNG of a render), raw pixel buffers. HEIC is read but not written. Nothing writes camera RAW formats.
- **Metadata:** EXIF, ICC, XMP, IPTC carried verbatim; the report says what a container could not hold.
- **Hostile input:** every parser is fuzzed under AddressSanitizer.

## 8. Measured (Intel i7-14700F, 8 threads, unless noted)

| Task | Result |
|---|---|
| Canon CR2 (35.6 MB) → lossless DNG, whole sensor | 28.3 MB in 0.31 s, mosaic bit-identical |
| JPEG → JPEG XL repack | 8.0 → 6.5 MB (−19%), reversible to the byte |
| 16-bit PNG (104 MB) → AVIF 10-bit 4:4:4, Iq q90 | 10.8 MB in 3.6 s |
| 24 MP JPEG → AVIF Iq q70, speed 6 | 4.30 MB in about 1.9 s |
| 102 MP Fujifilm RAF → scene-linear develop | 4.9 s, 1.49 GB peak |
| 2048 px HDR preview of a 24 MP edit from the master cache | 0.49 s |

- AVIF with AV1's still-image tuning (Iq) is 7–13% smaller than the default tuning at equal SSIMULACRA2 on photographs, about the size of x265 HEIC there, and 10–20% smaller than HEIC on graphics and HDR.
- iPhone HEIC: held to Apple's own renders of eleven photos (base within 2 eight-bit codes; HDR mean within 1 ten-bit PQ code).

## 9. Design principles

- The caller decides; the engine reports. No guessing, no silent defaults.
- Determinism: the same request gives the same bytes at any thread count; seeded randomness reproduces.
- What you see is what you export: a rendered region equals the same region cut from the full render, byte for byte.
- Honest loss accounting: the report states every rounding and anything it could not write.
